rules.category: Legal interviews and explainers
rules.rules:
Use for GLK interviews and legal explainers. Before editing new raw footage, ask “Would you like me to apply GLK Law Firm Styles?” unless the user has already selected it. Preserve source media, approved drafts and past revisions. Save new iterations separately and generalize confirmed feedback into a new preset version.

Picture and pacing

- Start with the speaker’s strongest clear thought. Trim dead air, false starts and redundant takes while preserving meaning, breaths and continuity. Favor clean cuts and restrained eased push-ins where emphasis warrants them.
- Use stable, full-frame footage of GLK people, offices and activities that directly illustrate the current narration. Reframe for the delivery aspect ratio and check every cut for jumpy motion and unintended black edges. Return to the speaker at a natural sentence or clause boundary. Use the word timing and the note’s draft frame to determine cut points.
- Keep brand elements consistent with white, gold #C19733 and navy #2A3643. Use a quietly animated name graphic below the caption area. Keep the product-liability callout above the head where applicable. Use the supplied GLK end card and avoid a frozen talking-head hold before it.

Captions and audio

- Use Poppins Bold upright. Set short, large white phrases with a soft dark shadow and limited muted gold emphasis. Keep captions centered chest-high, immediately below the chin, within mobile safe margins and clear of the face and lower third. Check names and titles against the supplied brand assets.
- Align each phrase and any word emphasis to the spoken words. Use gentle reveals and stable captions without visible flicker. Review the opening closely. Prefer a few purposeful highlights over decorative italic typography.
- Keep the original dialogue forward. Use quiet warm documentary or restrained corporate instrumental music with light percussion, fades at both ends and ducking under speech. Audition the mix on headphones and phone speakers so the music is audible and speech stays clear. Use soft timed sound accents and very short warm edge leaks only where they support an edit.

QA before delivery

- Compare each timestamped instruction against the rendered version with a frame on either side of the edit. Keep unapplied notes open.
- Watch the full rendered draft independently at normal playback, then step through cut points. Confirm pacing, caption sync, reading size and chin clearance, lower-third placement, crop and B-roll stability. Listen for intelligible dialogue, music balance, intentional SFX, and smooth fades. Check the first and last frames as well as all overlays and transitions.
- Run the automated decode, timing and audio-peak checks. Investigate black and freeze findings against the intended cut and distinguish deliberate graphics holds from accidental holds. Correct issues and rerun QA before export. Confirm that the downloaded file matches the newest review render and retain approved prior drafts.

## Delivery format and reference check

- For GLK Instagram Reels, establish a 1080 × 1920 portrait timeline before editing. Review the supplied brand files, a captioned example and the project-specific cues before choosing crops, typography or transitions. Apply the brief's specific ending and graphics choices to each reel.
- A source trim is an intake preview. A review draft needs the requested storytelling, graphics, timed captions, cuts, sound mix and mobile composition. Verify the actual rendered dimensions and square pixels, then check picture and caption timing at the opening, each insert and the ending.
